Chapter 1: Setting Out on the Journey Back Through Time
There’s something comforting about digging into your family’s past—maybe flipping through old photos, or listening to those stories your grandparents used to tell.
But what if tracing your family tree didn’t stop a few generations back? What if you could follow those branches all the way to the very beginning of life itself?
Imagine standing at the tip of a gigantic, sprawling tree. Every fork in its branches marks a moment when lives took different paths, and every single leaf represents a living being. That’s where we start—a journey into the past that doesn’t move forward, but instead walks backward, step by step, from today to the dawn of life.
The idea behind this is surprisingly simple, but honestly, it’s kind of mind-blowing: if you go back far enough, every living thing shares a common ancestor.
Now, we’ll begin with humans—not because we’re the main event, but because it’s familiar ground. From there, the path winds through the ages, and along the way, we’ll meet fellow travelers—other species—at those special moments when their history and ours once joined. Each of these meetings is like a family reunion, a gentle reminder that the line between “us” and “them” isn’t as permanent as it seems.
I remember a teacher once telling a curious group of students that the story of life isn’t a straight line, but more like a branching river. The students, who’d always pictured evolution as a ladder with humans on top, were taken aback. The teacher drew a tree on the chalkboard—every branch leading back to a trunk, and even the trunk splitting and joining with others further down. Suddenly, the students saw that this tree didn’t have a top or a bottom. Just endless, connected branches.
This journey isn’t about finding one single ancestor. It’s about discovering the deep connections that tie all living things together. Along the way, we’ll hit “rendezvous points”—moments in the distant past where different lineages come together. At each of these stops, the travelers pause, take a look around, and recognize their distant relatives. The journey celebrates both the incredible diversity of life, and the unity that runs beneath it all.
As we set off, something becomes clear: evolution isn’t just about fossils or DNA. It’s about how we see ourselves, and our place among all living things.
Most of us grow up thinking that humans are somehow separate, special, even inevitable. But as we walk backward along this ancient path, it becomes obvious—we’re just one tiny twig on a vast and ancient tree.
And you know what? That realization is humbling, but also deeply reassuring. It shows that every living thing on Earth shares the same story—a story that began billions of years ago, and is still being written today.
